runs.question: What penalty does the NIST AI RMF set for an organization that chooses not to adopt it?

answer.text:
The AI RMF documents don't set any penalty for organizations that decline to adopt it. I found no passage describing a sanction, fine, or other consequence for non-adoption.

The framework's own description points the other way. NIST describes it as a resource that organizations can choose to use. The text says it is intended to be voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific, and use-case agnostic. The document also says that use of the AI RMF alone will not lead to these changes or provide the appropriate incentives, which suggests that adoption depends on an organization's own accountability structures rather than on any external penalty.

This answer covers only the AI RMF (document 1). I did not search the other NIST, OMB, or White House documents for penalties tied to adoption, so I can't rule out that another document addresses this.
